questions: Should the function wait indefinitely for the background process to complete, or is there a timeout after which it should return a specific code (e.g., kill the process and return an error)?
If the URL contains spaces or special characters, should it be shell-escaped, or is it passed raw to the command?
Is the return code always the exit code of the subprocess, or should it be transformed (e.g., negative for signals, custom codes for platform errors)?
Should the function handle cases where the default browser command fails to start (e.g., FileNotFoundError) by raising an exception or returning a specific code?
Does 'background process' mean the function must not block the caller, or is it acceptable to block until the browser opens (as the reference does)?
Should the function validate the URL format (e.g., starts with http://) before attempting to open, or pass any string to the OS command?
On Windows with 'shell=True', should the command be a single string ('start https://...') or a list as shown?
If the browser opens successfully but the subprocess exits immediately (e.g., on some Linux setups), should the function return 0 or wait for the browser to close?
